$comment: Per-harness probe plan consumed by probe.mjs. Placeholders: {BIN} {HOME} {SCRATCH} {CWD} {PROMPT} {MODEL} {TSX} {CLI} {WORKTREE}. Env values written as "$OPENROUTER_API_KEY" are resolved from the runner's process.env at spawn time and are never written to any output file.

mcp_server.$comment: Timmy's own MCP server. The literal task spec says `npx tsx <cli.ts> mcp serve`; tsx is not on PATH globally and npx from a foreign cwd would block on an interactive install prompt, so the worktree's node_modules/.bin/tsx is used directly (same program).

jcode.kind: local coding agent (Rust binary, background daemon + client)
jcode.model_route: OpenRouter via built-in `openrouter` provider; key read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY env
jcode.isolation: JCODE_HOME={HOME} + --socket {HOME}/jcode.sock so a private daemon is used; user's ~/.jcode untouched

mcp.note: jcode reads <JCODE_HOME>/mcp.json ({"servers":{...}} shape, same as the user's real ~/.jcode/mcp.json). Written into the isolated JCODE_HOME before the daemon starts; --mcp-tools eager forces exposure.

jcode.mcp_model_note: mcp_client runs on anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 instead of gemini-3.7-flash: with Gemini the harness DID load and forward Timmy's MCP tools, but Google rejected the whole request because Timmy's timmy_promo_apply tool declares `beats: {type:'array'}` without `items` (function_declarations[35].parameters.properties[beats].items: missing field). That is a Timmy schema bug, not a harness limitation; Anthropic accepts the schema.

opencode.model_route: OpenRouter via `-m openrouter/<model>`; key read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY env
opencode.isolation: OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR={HOME} replaces ~/.config/opencode; project-level opencode.json in the probe cwd for MCP. Claude-Code compat + external skills disabled so the user's ~/.claude skill library (which pushed a bare PONG to ~159k input tokens in a smoke test) is not injected.

mcp.note: Project-scoped opencode.json in the probe's temp cwd (never the user's ~/.config/opencode).

opencode.mcp_model_note: mcp_client runs on anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 (see jcode.mcp_model_note: Gemini rejects Timmy's timmy_promo_apply schema).

pi.model_route: Ollama (http://localhost:11434/v1, openai-completions) exactly as the user runs it (memory: pi-ollama-launchers); cloud model routed through the local daemon. First attempt used qwen3-coder-next:cloud, which Ollama Cloud reports as retired since 2026-07-15 (HTTP 410), so glm-5.3-flash:cloud (verified alive with a direct curl) is used with thinking off.
pi.isolation: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR={HOME} (fresh agent dir with models.json/settings.json written by the runner). The user's real ~/.pi/agent currently fails to start: settings.json packages include npm:@astrofoundry/pi-astro whose global npm install is broken, and pi aborts before parsing args (even with -ne).

mcp.note: pi has no built-in MCP client; MCP arrives via the pi-mcp-adapter extension. The user's copy at /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/pi-mcp-adapter is loaded explicitly with -e (no install), and the server is declared in a project-local .mcp.json inside the temp cwd. Caveat found while running: that adapter is built against @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.1 (a second pi install at ~/.local/bin/pi -> ~/.hermes/node/bin/pi), not the pinned /opt/homebrew/bin/pi (@mariozechner 0.73.1), and fails to load with 'Cannot find module @earendil-works/pi-ai/compat'.

hermes.kind: local agent (Python, Nous Hermes Agent); bin is a bash wrapper around ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes
hermes.model_route: OpenRouter via --provider openrouter -m <model>; key read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY env
hermes.isolation: HERMES_HOME={HOME} (fresh home, own config.yaml/auth.json/state.db); user's ~/.hermes untouched

setup_files.text:
mcp_servers:
  timmy:
    command: {TSX}
    args:
      - {CLI}
      - mcp
      - serve
    enabled: true

mcp.note: The mcp_servers block is written straight into <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml of the isolated home (the same {command,args,enabled} shape `hermes mcp add` saves). First pass tried `hermes mcp add`: it connected and listed all 23 Timmy tools but then hit input() -> EOFError on the no-TTY confirmation and printed 'Cancelled.' without saving, so `mcp add` is interactive-only.

hermes.mcp_model_note: mcp_client runs on anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 (see jcode.mcp_model_note: Gemini rejects Timmy's timmy_promo_apply schema).
hermes.tool_call_note: -z one-shot prints only the final answer, so tool calls are not visible in the transcript; file_edits (file on disk) is the hard evidence.

openhands.kind: local coding agent CLI (Python, OpenHands SDK); bin is a uv-tool python entry script
openhands.model_route: OpenRouter via LiteLLM: LLM_MODEL=openrouter/<model>, LLM_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, LLM_API_KEY from env, enabled with --override-with-envs
openhands.isolation: HOME={SCRATCH}/fakehome plus OPENHANDS_PERSISTENCE_DIR={HOME}. A fake HOME is required, not just nice: with the real HOME the SDK crawls ~/.agents/skills (1,632 skill symlinks, 34,572 files, 280 MB on this machine; no env override exists) and had not finished loading skills after 120 s in three attempts, and it also writes ~/.openhands/cache/skills. The public-skills git clone is copied from the user's existing cache into the fake HOME so no network clone is needed. User's ~/.openhands config untouched.

mcp.note: `openhands mcp add` writes <OPENHANDS_PERSISTENCE_DIR>/mcp.json in the isolated dir. Measured outcome: openhands spawns Timmy's server and discovers its tools, then aborts the conversation with ConversationErrorEvent TypeError "Field 'kind' of class 'MCPTimmyGenRunAction' overrides symbol of same name in a parent class" — Timmy's timmy_gen_run tool has an input parameter literally named `kind`, which collides with the OpenHands SDK's pydantic `kind` discriminator on generated MCP action classes. So the client exists and connects, but no tool call can be made against Timmy's server as-is (rename the parameter, or the SDK must namespace it).

openhands.mcp_model_note: mcp_client runs on openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 via LLM_MODEL (see jcode.mcp_model_note: Gemini rejects Timmy's timmy_promo_apply schema).

minds.kind: NOT a local coding agent: '@animocabrands/minds-cli' is a JSON client for hosted 'Minds' conversations (send/history/events); tools, files and browsing (if any) run on the remote Mind, not on this machine
minds.model_route: none locally; requires MINDS_BUILDER_API_KEY (not set anywhere in this environment) and a hosted Mind alias
minds.isolation: no config written; only read-only diagnostics run
minds.null_reason: minds is a thin client for a hosted agent; with no MINDS_BUILDER_API_KEY nothing can be sent, and even when configured the tool/file/browser work would execute remotely, so local file_edits/tool_use/browser/sandbox are not measurable here
